races.name: Sky Sports Racing Juvenile Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Hello Garda
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's gelding boasts the most convincing recent form in the field with a win and a third on good ground over staying trips, making it the standout closer on merit; it is a natural hold-up horse whose true style means it will need the pace to collapse or a clean passage in the straight, so treat its mapping into midfield as a compression artefact rather than its preferred position.
runners_data.comment: Hello Garda arrives in winning form, scoring last time out and third two starts back, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour; the chief concern is 161 lb on his back after a 43-day absence.

runners_data.name: Timely Salute
runners_data.note: Max Comley's charge won over 17f on good ground last time, ticking the going and trip boxes neatly, and brings a hold-up profile that suits a race with a genuine finisher's kick; the 50-day absence and patchy wider form record means it needs to show it retains that level before being trusted fully.
runners_data.comment: Timely Salute heads this seven-runner field on the back of a recent victory and has run over today's trip before; at 161 lb he carries a weight to respect, but his rating of 96 marks him as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Jerseygeordie
runners_data.note: Harry Derham's yard is in good recent form (T14: 2/3) and this three-year-old arrives fresh after 87 days off, though a flat-track form string on standard ground offers limited evidence it will translate to hurdles on good; at heart a horse that wants to come from off the pace, it has been squeezed toward midfield simply because the field is overloaded with closers, not because it is a natural prominent racer.
runners_data.comment: Jerseygeordie makes his debut here after an 87-day absence, arriving unexposed and open to plenty of improvement; lightly raced and yet to score, he is one to watch as his profile fills out.

runners_data.name: Moment Of Light
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner and the key pace anchor, ridden by Harry Skelton for a yard firing at 8/24 over 14 days; its four wins have come on standard ground, and while good-ground form is thinner (0W1P in 4 runs), controlling the race unchallenged is a significant tactical asset that compensates for any going query.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Moment Of Light arrives here after 107 days off for a trainer firing at 33% in the last fortnight, and carrying 154 lb, he represents a yard in red-hot form with plenty still to find out about him.

runners_data.name: Nicolai
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland's runner was seen just 10 days ago, arrives quickly back, and carries a fading-in-the-finish flag that is a material concern in a race likely run at a pace that will test stamina in the closing stages; though genuinely a hold-up horse by inclination, the redistribution toward midfield reflects field compression rather than any natural boldness from the front.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Nicolai is yet to win in his last two starts — including a pull-up — but the 10-day turnaround suggests connections are keen, and at 154 lb there is plenty to work with from a lightly raced profile.

runners_data.name: Rajbello
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien, who has two winners from ten runners over 14 days, saddles this gelding just nine days after its last run, suggesting it is in good order, but its form on good ground is thin (2 from 9 qualifying runs, no wins) and it has never shown the ability to dominate; like several others in this field it is a true hold-up type pushed forward on the map by necessity, not by preference.
runners_data.comment: Rajbello makes his debut here, an unexposed gelding carrying 154 lb just nine days after his last appearance, with his potential entirely unknown and every reason to think improvement is firmly on the cards.

runners_data.name: Zooter
runners_data.note: Sam Twiston-Davies takes the ride for Jack Jones on a horse with a model good-ground profile (9 from 11 qualifying runs) and a consistent set of placed efforts at staying trips; a natural hold-up horse, it has the tactical flexibility to track closer than its preferred position if the pace invites it, and its consistency makes it the most likely beneficiary if Moment Of Light comes back to the field.
runners_data.comment: Zooter has experience of today's going and arrives here fresh on a 27-day break, with our rating of 80 placing him second among seven — a solid threat despite being yet to score in recent starts, and the main risk is that single-run sample leaving his current level hard to assess.

races.paceDynamic: Moment Of Light is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner juvenile hurdle and, ridden by Harry Skelton for the in-form Dan Skelton yard, will be allowed to dictate a controlled, uncontested pace on good ground at Newton Abbot. With no rivals likely to seriously challenge for the lead, Moment Of Light can set a measured tempo that suits a relaxed traveller rather than a finisher with a big kick, making this a race won from the front or from a close-tracking position off a sustainable gallop. The field is heavily stacked with hold-up types — Hello Garda, Jerseygeordie, Nicolai, and Rajbello are all redistributed into midfield on the map, meaning they are genuine closers forced to compress toward the pace, not natural prominent racers — and this bunching in the middle of the field will limit their ability to produce the sustained late run their style demands. This race shape strongly favours Moment Of Light and any horse capable of tracking closely in second or third, as the modest, self-set pace means those racing prominently will get the first run, and true hold-up horses are unlikely to generate enough momentum late to reel in a relaxed, well-placed leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Moment Of Light Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Moment Of Light bowls along at a comfortable clip with no rival prepared to go with it, setting a controlled pace that rewards front-running precision.
scenarios.body: Harry Skelton produces a confident front-running display, controlling the race from the first hurdle and quickening at the business end before tired rivals can close; the Skelton yard's 8/24 T14 strike rate underlines this is a live player.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or close-tracking horse travels sweetly just off Moment Of Light and produces a sharper jump at the last to go past.
scenarios.body: The steady pace allows a fluid jumper sitting second or third to coast into contention without burning energy; Zooter's consistent form figures and good-ground profile make it the most logical beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or a gap opens in the straight allowing one of the genuine closers to find a run and pick off a fading leader.
scenarios.body: Hello Garda, trained by John Joseph Hanlon and carrying the best recent form (1,3 figures over similar trips on good ground), is the most credible finisher in the field if traffic clears in time; Timely Salute, a winner on good ground over 17f, also has the profile to finish strongly if the front-runner weakens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Into Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Moment Of Light jumps poorly or is headed early, sparking a contested pace that blows the race wide open.
scenarios.body: Without a reliable pace anchor, several rivals scramble for position and the race becomes a test of jumping accuracy rather than stamina or finishing speed; in this scenario Jerseygeordie or Rajbello, both from active stables, could benefit from an unpredictable sequence of events.

watchPoints.text: Moment Of Light's jumping must be monitored from the outset — any early error under Harry Skelton could hand the race leadership to an unprepared rival and transform the entire pace shape.

Hello Garda is the most dangerous closer on form but will need a completely clean run through what could be a congested midfield pack of similarly styled hold-up horses; watch for a traffic problem turning in.

Nicolai is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish and races just 10 days after its last run — if it is prominent early and weakens, it could cause interference for runners travelling behind it at a critical stage.

Zooter's jockey Sam Twiston-Davies may choose to press Moment Of Light early given the lack of other prominent types — if he does, the dynamic shifts from a lone leader to a two-horse race from the front and that changes the calculus for closers.

The redistribution of four genuine hold-up horses into midfield means the middle of the race will be unusually compressed — watch for a rough passage on the final bend as several closers simultaneously try to find their run.

races.name: Race Against Waste Maiden Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Crystal Mariner
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer with solid Good-ground form (won on sim-going 1W3P), stepping up slightly in distance here — Paddy Hanlon's claim is useful and the style suits a truly run race created by the two front-runners duelling out in front.

runners_data.name: Happy Chandler
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner fitted with headgear, this horse must lead to be seen at its best; Good ground suits and the form shows a win at 10f on Good, but the step up to 2m1f and direct pace rivalry with John Galt could find this horse out in the final quarter-mile.

runners_data.name: Crackalackin
runners_data.note: Luke Scott's 3lb claim helps a horse that has been admirably consistent at this trip, placing four times in five at 2m on Good — a prominent pitch just off the pace could see this four-year-old prove very hard to pass if the leaders overdo it.

runners_data.name: Explode
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride on a horse whose two wins came at 12f on Good ground, but its natural racing style is closer to prominent-to-midfield than genuine hold-up; redistributed to midfield on the map due to field congestion at the rear, its chance is tempered by the likelihood it races out of its most comfortable position.

runners_data.name: John Galt
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's runner has two wins from two starts on Good-ish ground and is a confirmed front-runner by style, wearing a tongue tie — 64 days off the track is worth noting, but the trainer has landed 2 from 10 in the 14-day window and the horse is well-handed for an up-front challenge.

runners_data.name: Pay Attention
runners_data.note: A hold-up type from Sara Bradstock's yard that has placed four times in five starts on Good ground at shorter distances, stepping up considerably in trip here — the form shows durability but the 49 days off and significant step to 2m1f introduce genuine uncertainty about whether the stamina will extend to the longer test.

races.paceDynamic: John Galt and Happy Chandler are both confirmed front-runners in a field of just six, setting up a directly contested early duel that should produce an honest, sustained gallop throughout. John Galt (Liam Harrison, Fergal O'Brien) has been tracking prominent positions in recent starts and will look to lead, while Happy Chandler (Harry Reed) has headgear noted and a clear front-running profile — neither is likely to concede the lead without a fight. Behind them, Crackalackin should slot into a prominent tracking role, with Crystal Mariner, Pay Attention, and Explode operating further back, though this field holds more hold-up types than can all get a genuine position at the rear — Explode is the most likely to be shuffled out of its natural style, with Crystal Mariner and Pay Attention better placed to find clean air from the back. The contested pace between two genuine front-runners on Good ground over 2m1f strongly favours hold-up or prominent-tracking types who can conserve energy early and arrive late with a sustained challenge, rather than those who must go with the pace from the outset.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If John Galt and Happy Chandler push each other along from the front and set a true pace that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other off, setting up a truly run race where horses held up or tracking at a comfortable distance can produce a telling late challenge jumping the final flights. Crystal Mariner and Pay Attention, genuine hold-up types with good form on Good ground, are best placed to capitalise on a strongly run race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Controls Pace
scenarios.trigger: If one of John Galt or Happy Chandler dominates from the front and the other is unable to match the early tempo.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner sets a more controlled gallop, reducing the pace pressure and giving the leader a greater chance of lasting to the line, particularly if John Galt can use his O'Brien stability and Good-ground course form to dictate on his own terms. Crackalackin, tracking prominently, would also be well positioned to pounce if the leader fades late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel peters out mid-race and a prominent tracker saves enough energy to outstay the leaders.
scenarios.body: Crackalackin has consistent placed form at this trip on Good ground and has been running well from a prominent position, meaning a steadier-than-expected race could play to its stamina and consistency. Dr Richard Newland's patient placement of this horse at 2m+ on Good conditions makes it the most natural beneficiary of a moderately run pace from prominent ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Fails to Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the race is run at a stop-start tempo that bunches the field and nullifies the hold-up horses' late runs.
scenarios.body: In a falsely run or muddled race, hold-up horses Crystal Mariner, Pay Attention, and the redistributed Explode may find themselves with too much ground to make up over the final flight. The front-runners and prominent types who have preserved their position through a tactical affair would benefit most in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether John Galt or Happy Chandler blinks first going to the first hurdle — if both commit fully to the lead, the pace could be fierce enough to set up a winning opportunity for Crystal Mariner or Pay Attention from off the pace.

Happy Chandler's stamina at 2m1f is unproven having run all recent form at 10f — if this horse ties up turning for home after a contested lead, it could bring John Galt back to the field and hand the race to a tracker.

Explode, despite Harry Cobden's presence, may never settle into its preferred position given the congestion at the rear — if it ends up racing too prominently against its natural style, its finishing effort could be compromised.

Pay Attention is stepping markedly up in trip from 8-10f to 2m1f — the form on Good ground is consistent but this extra distance over hurdles is a significant unknown and worth monitoring for any signs of the horse finding it tough late on.

Crackalackin arrives on just 23 days' rest with four consecutive placed efforts at this trip — if it can slot in second or third early without being drawn into the pace duel, Luke Scott's 3lb claim and the horse's consistency make it a quiet danger throughout.

races.name: St. Austell Brewery Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Melton Mossy
runners_data.note: Holds dual Good-ground wins over 16-19f trips and solid course form, but has been off 108 days and carries a natural hold-up style that relies on a strong gallop to be at his most effective — Adam Wedge will need Juggernaut to set a genuinely searching pace to deliver him late.
runners_data.comment: Melton Mossy landed a winner two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a clear threat at the head of our ratings; the main concern is whether 108 days off the track has left him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Saint Polo
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins on Good ground at 17-18f show sharp current form, and Luke Scott's 3lb claim is meaningful here; a true hold-up horse who will be closest to Juggernaut among the closers given his freshness (10 days) and strong trainer-in-form stats (1/13 T14).
runners_data.comment: Saint Polo arrives in superb nick, winning three of his last five starts including a hat-trick earlier in that sequence, and he has run over today's trip and going before. Carrying 163 lb is the one query, but his form trajectory makes him hard to oppose.

runners_data.name: Juggernaut
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner who gets to bowl along uncontested, though his STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) reflects that he has previously raced in a more prominent role and his record shows eight consecutive places without a win — the key question is whether he can convert front-running control into a victory.
runners_data.comment: Juggernaut has been knocking at the door with two seconds and two thirds in recent starts, and at 13 days he arrives fresh over a trip and going he has already experienced; the concern is that he remains yet to win, and converting that consistency into a win is the test.

runners_data.name: Most Wanted
runners_data.note: Bounced back to winning form 11 days ago and carries a visor for the first time today; his natural hold-up style means he'll be finishing from the rear despite his midfield map position, and both the STYLE_FIT discount and his light weight (146lbs, OR 87) highlight the handicapping gap he needs to bridge.
runners_data.comment: Most Wanted arrives here in cracking heart after finishing second last time out and a winner four starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going stands him in good stead; the main concern is that seventh two starts back hints he can blow hot and cold.

runners_data.name: Miss Denver
runners_data.note: A consistent performer who has finished second in four of her last six starts on Good ground, suggesting she finds a way to be competitive without always winning; Sam Twiston-Davies rides for a strong pairing, but her true hold-up profile and the absence of a win signal she may finish a creditable place without threatening the front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts despite a string of placed efforts, Miss Denver has experience over today's trip and conditions but is ranked last on our figures, and at 145 lb she faces a stiff task to finally get her head in front.

races.paceDynamic: Juggernaut is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and, with no genuine pace rival to harry him, Chad Bament can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits over this 2m½f trip on Good ground at Newton Abbot. The remainder of the field — Melton Mossy, Saint Polo, Most Wanted, and Miss Denver — are all hold-up types by profile, meaning the race is likely to develop into a procession behind Juggernaut before the hold-up brigade make their moves from the home turn. It is worth noting that Most Wanted and Miss Denver are true hold-up horses whose redistribution to midfield on the map reflects the concentration of off-the-pace runners, not a change in their actual racing behaviour. This race shape — a lone, uncontested pace-setter on Good ground with a field of closers tracking from behind — strongly favours a prominent hold-up horse who can travel efficiently in Juggernaut's slipstream and produce a clean jump at the last, rather than a deep closer who needs a genuine strongly-run gallop to reel in a fresher front-runner.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Juggernaut Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Juggernaut bowls along in front at a sustainable clip and the hold-up horses are left with too much to do.
scenarios.body: Juggernaut sets a controlled, uncontested gallop and Chad Bament dictates the fractions, ensuring his mount jumps cleanly and conserves energy to the line; the closers are forced to pick off ground gradually but find the leader has stolen a decisive march.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If Juggernaut's stamina gives out on the final climb and the hold-up horses unleash a strong finishing run.
scenarios.body: Saint Polo, who has been in flying form winning three of his last four on Good ground, and Melton Mossy, a course type, are ideally suited to picking up from off the pace if Juggernaut's effort flattens out; this is the shape that most benefits the horse carrying the sharpest recent form and best fitness profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Sit-and-Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up horses forces their way closer to Juggernaut than expected and pounces before the final fence.
scenarios.body: Most Wanted or Miss Denver, travelling handily rather than off the pace as is their natural tendency, could steal a march on deeper hold-up rivals if the pace is genuinely steady enough to allow them to track Juggernaut closely; however, both carry the STYLE_FIT discount and visor/tongue-tie headgear angles temper confidence in this outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Sorts Field
scenarios.trigger: If the Good ground rides slower than expected and a grinding stamina test materialises over the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Melton Mossy, who has course form and winning form over marathon trips on Good ground, would be best suited to an attritional finish; Saint Polo's consistent Good-ground form also gives him claims, though this scenario requires conditions to be materially more testing than the going report suggests.

watchPoints.text: Juggernaut sets the tempo entirely on his own terms — if Chad Bament is allowed to control fractions throughout, he becomes very difficult to peg back and his eight consecutive placings suggest he is long overdue a win.

Saint Polo's three consecutive wins and trainer form make him the most dangerous closer in the field — watch whether Luke Scott positions him closer than his nominal hold-up tag suggests, exploiting the steady pace from just off Juggernaut's shoulder.
Melton Mossy's 108-day absence is the critical unknown; if he returns below peak, his hold-up profile requires a stronger gallop than Juggernaut is likely to deliver, leaving him with too much to do.

Most Wanted debuts in a visor today — first-time headgear in a small field on Good ground can sharpen a hold-up horse's early focus and may see him travel more prominently than expected, though his STYLE_FIT tag tempers expectations.

With four genuine hold-up horses and only one pace-setter, watch early positioning at the first fence — any runner who jumps into a tracking role directly behind Juggernaut gains a significant tactical advantage over those forced to make up ground from further back.

races.name: Devonport Royal Dockyard Social Club Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Jager Time
runners_data.note: Won over 26f on good ground most recently, form reads 1-4321 with strong similar-going record (11/14), and at 7 years old sits at the peak stamina age for this trip; a hold-up type by trade but maps into tracking territory here which may actually suit if he can latch onto My Girl Katie from close range.
runners_data.comment: Jager Time arrives on the back of a win last time out, and his recent sequence shows two wins in his last five starts, underlining consistent competitiveness; carrying 168 lb after a 50-day break is the chief concern, though he has experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Fairlawn Skipper
runners_data.note: Back just seven days after his last run which warrants monitoring for freshness, and his recent form includes an unfinished run (U) and a fall (1) which raises jumping reliability flags; his best effort was a win over 22f on good, so this 3m2½f trip is a genuine stamina question, though good ground suits.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win two starts back before unseating last time, Fairlawn Skipper has experience of today's going and returns quickly on seven days' rest with a trainer firing at 26% over the last fortnight — that stable form makes him hard to oppose despite the hefty 167 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Masterdream
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap applied and runs in the colours of a trainer who has been quiet over the last 14 days (0/9); his best form sits over much shorter (14f wins in his history) and at 9 years old returning off 17 days, the stamina for 3m2½f is questionable — he is a hold-up horse by inclination but the field density means he cannot get as far back as he would like.
runners_data.comment: Masterdream arrives on the back of a third last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a solid platform at 160 lb, though the pulled up effort two starts back is the one rival backers will point to as the main concern.

runners_data.name: My Girl Katie
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: three wins from three over this exact trip and ground combination in recent form, handled by a 7lb claiming apprentice which partially offsets her rise in the weights; her 9-year-old frame is proven at the trip and the absence of any pace rival means she controls entirely — the STYLE_FIT flag is a structural note only and does not undermine what is a compelling front-running profile for this race.
runners_data.comment: Three wins on the bounce reads brilliantly, but My Girl Katie carries a hefty 155 lb and our rating of 88 leaves her trailing the principals in this field; she has run over today's trip and going before, which at least removes any obvious questions about conditions.

runners_data.name: Bashful Boy
runners_data.note: Tongue-and-bit combination applied, and his recent form includes a pulled-up run (P) and a zero (0) suggesting jumping or motivation issues; a 10-year-old returning off 47 days, he has been placed over shorter trips on good ground but 3m2½f is untested in his recent history — his hold-up tendency cannot be fully expressed in this field shape.
runners_data.comment: Rated highest of the seven runners here and has run on today's going before, Bashful Boy shaped with clear promise when third two starts back, giving reason to think he can go close again; yet to score in recent starts and that pulled-up effort four runs ago remains the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Henry Box Brown
runners_data.note: Won over 23f on good ground most recently and carries a decent recent form figure of 1, handled by Adam Wedge who rides him well at this level; his natural instinct is to come from off the pace but the compressed field means he will be nearer the action than usual, which could either help or unsettle his rhythm — 53 days since last run is worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying 143 lb after a 53-day absence, Henry Box Brown is hard to fancy despite winning last time out; he has experience of today's going, but his overall recent form — two sixths, an unseated, and a fourth in his last five starts — makes a case against him.

runners_data.name: Alberts Bay
runners_data.note: Consistent in form figures (3-6-3-7-3) but those thirds and sixths suggest a horse that arrives at the finish without ever quite threatening; James Best takes the ride for a trainer with a thin recent book (0/1 last 14 days), and on good ground he has a solid enough record (4/5) — a hold-up horse that needs things to go wrong for others rather than going right for him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Alberts Bay is hard to fancy on ratings alone, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a sharp 11-day turnaround carrying 142 lb.

races.paceDynamic: My Girl Katie is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no other horse likely to seriously contest the early lead, she will stride into a comfortable, sustainable gallop from the outset over this 3m2½f trip on good ground at Newton Abbot. The pace will be honest but controlled — a single-file procession is likely through the early stages, with My Girl Katie dictating fractions and the remainder of the field, led by Jager Time and Fairlawn Skipper, tracking at varying distances behind. This field carries a significant clustering of genuine hold-up types — Masterdream, Bashful Boy, Henry Box Brown, and Alberts Bay have all been redistributed forward on the map simply because there is no room for them at the rear in a seven-runner field, but their true preference is to race from the back, meaning the shape may look more compressed than it truly is. With one horse controlling a steady gallop unchallenged, this race shape strongly favours a prominently-ridden or pace-pressing profile — a horse that sits close enough to My Girl Katie to respond when she inevitably quickens from the front, rather than one that must find ground from a genuine hold-up position late in a race where the gallop may not be strong enough to bring closers into it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: My Girl Katie Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If My Girl Katie secures the lead uncontested and sets a controlled, honest gallop that she is never seriously challenged to increase.
scenarios.body: She bowls along from the front on her favoured good ground, drawing on a sequence of three recent wins over identical conditions and trip, and the lack of any rival willing to press her means she can conserve energy before kicking again at the business end.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Presser Overpowers
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or tracking horse applies sustained pressure from the home turn, grinding down My Girl Katie before she can fully exploit her front-running advantage.
scenarios.body: Jager Time or Fairlawn Skipper, tracking close enough in the early stages, moves up to challenge My Girl Katie approaching two out and the relentless grind of 3m2½f finally tells on the front-runner; the presser's superior staying power wins out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finisher Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a run-in for a horse coming from off the pace, and one of the redistributed hold-up types manages to get closer to its natural running position than expected.
scenarios.body: A horse such as Henry Box Brown or Masterdream, if allowed to settle further back than the map suggests and finding a strongly-run race, picks off tired rivals in the closing stages; however this scenario is structurally undermined by the fact that most hold-up types here are racing out of their true role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If the race degenerates through jumping errors, fallers, or My Girl Katie going too fast too soon and the field strings out with multiple horses tiring before the last.
scenarios.body: A chaotic or attritional race where the last horse standing, rather than the fastest, takes it; any horse with sound jumping and basic stamina could profit, but form becomes almost irrelevant in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: My Girl Katie's jumping must be tracked from the front — if she makes a significant error at any hurdle with no rival to pressurise her into correcting, the race is immediately wide open and a presser like Jager Time or Fairlawn Skipper could capitalise.

Fairlawn Skipper ran just seven days ago and has an unfinished run (U) in recent form — watch in the paddock and early in the race for any sign that the quick turnaround has left him less than fully wound, which would compromise his ability to track close to the pace.

Masterdream and Bashful Boy both have tongue straps applied and will be forced to race further forward than their natural style allows — watch for either horse becoming unsettled or jumping raggedly in the early stages as a result of the unnatural positioning.

The 3m2½f trip is the longest test in this card at Newton Abbot and the stamina profiles of several runners are unproven at the distance — Alberts Bay, Bashful Boy, and Fairlawn Skipper have all operated mainly at shorter, so monitor whether any begin to struggle from three out onwards.

Henry Box Brown returns after 53 days off and won last time out — watch his early behaviour to gauge whether the break has left him fresh and sharp or just slightly ring-rusty, as his chance depends on travelling smoothly from a wide-ish position.

races.name: Par Inn Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Edelak
runners_data.note: Four-year-old in superb form (five wins from last six, including four consecutive 2m wins on Good), trained by Dan Skelton with Harry Skelton aboard — a high-class combination — though the STYLE_FIT tag notes it is racing slightly out of its most comfortable role; the confirmed front-runner sets the entire race shape and is the dominant force on ratings (OR 124).|
runners_data.comment: Edelak arrives on the back of a winning run and boasts four wins in his last six starts, with experience of today's distance and going working in his favour alongside a trainer firing at 33% in the last fortnight; the chief concern is 50 days off the track.

runners_data.name: War Correspondent
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old returning quickly after just seven days off (LR:7d), trained by John Joseph Hanlon with claimer Paddy Hanlon (5lb) in the saddle, which is a notable jockey discount; genuine hold-up horse with solid sim-going form (14/15) but a poor recent string (4U439F) and the short turnaround could blunt its finishing effort.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, War Correspondent nonetheless showed a third three starts back and returns quickly on seven days' rest, boasting experience over today's trip and going; at 163 lb he faces a stiff ask, but our rating of 128 marks him as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Arctic Voyage
runners_data.note: Strong profile for a four-year-old with OR 116 and excellent form figures (P1-121) including three wins on Good going — the sim-going stats (7/15, 3W5P) show it handles these conditions; 66 days off is worth monitoring for freshness, but Michael Blake's runner is a natural hold-up horse whose three recent course-distance wins at 17f suggest it will relish this trip and ground combination.|
runners_data.comment: Arctic Voyage arrives in fine nick, winning two of his last three starts and filling the runner-up spot in between, and he has experience of today's distance and going; the main risk is a 66-day absence, though his form peak suggests he retains plenty of ability at 160 lb.

runners_data.name: Ellerton
runners_data.note: Joe Tizzard's six-year-old won last time out (LR:11d) and holds Good-ground form (3W6P in nine runs on sim going), but its true hold-up style means it is unlikely to replicate its natural position in this race — pushed closer by the lack of other deep closers, it is operating somewhat against type, and the STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence in its ability to reproduce that profile here.|
runners_data.comment: Ellerton won last time out and was a second three starts back, boasting two wins in his last five starts and returning fit on just 11 days' rest; the main concern is that pulled-up effort sandwiched between, which remains the question mark over his consistency.

races.paceDynamic: Edelak is the sole confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field and will set the tempo from the front, with no other genuine pace-setter to pressure or challenge that position. On Good ground over 2m1f at Newton Abbot, a track that rewards those who travel well and jump fluently, Edelak's controlled lead is likely to be a sustainable, measured gallop rather than a breakneck pace — creating a sit-and-pounce dynamic for the three hold-up horses behind. War Correspondent, Arctic Voyage, and Ellerton are all hold-up types by profile, meaning the race shape strongly favours a horse who can track the leader efficiently and produce a decisive jump at the last — rewarding prominent-to-lead profiles or high-quality closers with strong finishes. This field carries more hold-up horses than the race map can accommodate at the rear; Ellerton is the most likely to be pushed closer than its natural style, as a pure hold-up operator redistributed to a midfield mapping, while War Correspondent and Arctic Voyage are the truest deep closers in the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Edelak Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak leads without pressure and dictates a comfortable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Edelak takes a relaxed lead on the Good ground, jumps fluently, and simply never faces enough pace pressure to be caught — Harry Skelton's quality allowing a switch-off and a well-timed injection of pace from the third-last. Horses who can travel prominently and stick on will pick off tiring hold-up types, but Edelak's class and form profile (five wins in six) make it very hard to reel in from deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak's pace is genuinely steady and a hold-up horse produces a strong jumping finish from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A truly pedestrian early pace compresses the field and leaves fresher legs amongst the closers, allowing War Correspondent or Arctic Voyage to sweep through on the bridle from the penultimate flight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Jumping Error Changes Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak makes a significant jumping mistake, handing the pace initiative to another runner mid-race.
scenarios.body: A fall or blunder from Edelak — whose form includes a recent F — would scramble the race shape entirely, promoting whichever horse is tracking closest into a front-running role they have not prepared for.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Ellerton Strikes Prominently
scenarios.trigger: If Ellerton, pushed forward out of its true hold-up style, secures an uncharacteristically prominent position and outstays rivals.
scenarios.body: Racing against its grain, Ellerton would need the pace to be just right and rivals to tie each other up; the STYLE_FIT discount and redistribution make this a low-probability shape, but its Good-ground form (three wins from nine on sim going) gives a slim theoretical case.

watchPoints.text: Watch Edelak's jumping closely — its recent form includes a fall (F in form string), and any mistake at a crucial Newton Abbot flight could unravel the entire predicted race shape.
War Correspondent returns after just seven days; if it shows signs of staleness or the claimer Paddy Hanlon (5lb) misjudges the hold-up timing, it may find itself too far back to mount a challenge.

Ellerton is being asked to race closer than its natural style — monitor whether Brendan Powell can engineer a forward position without burning too much fuel, or whether the horse simply cannot replicate its hold-up effectiveness.
Arctic Voyage is 66 days off track; a fresh jumper returning from absence on Good ground can sometimes be sluggish early — watch how quickly it settles into its rhythm in the early stages.

With only four runners on Good ground, the pace is entirely in Edelak's hands — if Harry Skelton chooses to crawl early and set up a sprint finish, the entire closing scenario probabilities shift upward for the hold-up trio.

races.name: Grandad Swales Happy 80th Birthday Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: My Cullen
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile suits this pace scenario well; Freddie Keighley partners a horse in fine recent form (ran 7 days ago), 9 wins/places from 15 on similar Good going, but the OR=93 top weight of 168lbs at a 6yo age is the key query.|
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in recent starts, including a second three runs back, My Cullen has run over today's trip and going and, rated 99, heads our rankings; winless in his last six, he needs to find more but the profile gives him every chance.

runners_data.name: Jetty May
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls sends out a 6yo mare fitted with tongue-tie and a hood, returning after 76 days off but boasting a win on Good over 22f and strong similar-going form (7/8 strike rate); her natural hold-up style slots perfectly into this pace shape and Paddy Hanlon claims 3lbs.|
runners_data.comment: Jetty May won three starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 95 marking her out as a leading player at the weights; the pull-up last time is the concern that must be answered.

runners_data.name: Hatos
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will contest the early lead directly with Mcgregors Charge; Joe Tizzard's 9yo returns after 76 days fitted with tongue-tie and cheekpieces, has consistent Good-ground form, but the 2m5f trip over fences at Newton Abbot and a pace battle from flag-fall are energy-sapping variables.|
runners_data.comment: Twice third and once second in his last three completed starts, Hatos boasts solid placing form and has experience over today's trip and going, while our rating of 88 marks him as a live threat; two consecutive non-completions and 76 days off are the concern.

runners_data.name: Mr McWhinny
runners_data.note: Won last time over a shorter 17f trip on Good and carries solid form credentials for T Ellis, but this is a genuine hold-up horse that has been pushed into a midfield position by race shape; racing materially out of role with a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 reduces confidence that it can reproduce its best.|
runners_data.comment: Mr McWhinny won two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, arriving fresh on 19 days' rest with his rating of 86 underlining strong claims; the worry is a fourth last time out suggests he can run hot and cold.

runners_data.name: Mcgregors Charge
runners_data.note: Polly Gundry's 8yo front-runner has finished placed in Good-ground races before but recent form reads P7-542 and OR=81 is the lowest in the field; sharing the pace-making duties with Hatos over 2m5f risks exhausting both and Jack Stenhouse claims 5lbs on a horse that may lack the class to sustain the battle.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Mcgregors Charge faces a stiff ask under 156 lb, though a runner-up finish last time out and experience over today's trip and going offer slim crumbs of comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Hatos and Mcgregors Charge are both confirmed front-runners and will clash for the lead from the jump, creating a genuinely contested gallop over 2m5f on Good turf at Newton Abbot. With two horses fighting for the same piece of track early, the pace is unlikely to be manufactured or false — expect an honest, sustained tempo that will begin to stretch the field from the second circuit. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can sit off the battle, conserve energy through the middle miles, and deliver a challenge at the final fences when the leaders are beginning to feel the pressure. The field holds more hold-up types than can all be accommodated at the rear — Mr McWhinny, a genuine hold-up horse, has been redistributed to midfield because Hatos and Mcgregors Charge will dominate the early positions, and Mr McWhinny is unlikely to secure its natural rearward berth; Hatos is almost certain to control the front rail.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Hatos and Mcgregors Charge burn each other up through a genuine pace battle, leaving the true hold-up horses to pounce late.
scenarios.body: The sustained duel between the two front-runners will drain their reserves on the long 2m5f trip, handing the race to those who tracked patiently in the second half of the field. My Cullen and Jetty May, both genuine hold-up types with solid form on Good going, are ideally profiled to pick up the pieces at the final fence and beyond.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Hatos repels Mcgregors Charge early and is allowed to dictate a controlled, bounced gallop from the front.
scenarios.body: Hatos has shown the ability to front-run and stay on at the OR=85 level, and if Mcgregors Charge is unable to match strides or backs off, Hatos could control tempo and conserve enough to hold on. A solo leader in Good ground over this trip can be surprisingly hard to peg back at Newton Abbot when the pace becomes measured rather than extreme.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the pace contest proves moderate rather than brutal, allowing Mr McWhinny to settle close enough to the action to produce a late challenge from its redistributed midfield slot.
scenarios.body: Mr McWhinny has winning form on Good going and showed a sharp turn of foot when last successful, but it is racing out of its natural hold-up role here and the style-fit discount is real. If the race tempo allows it to travel comfortably in the middle of the field rather than being stranded in rear, its OR=83 mark gives it a chance, though this shape is less likely given it is not in its preferred position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Claims All
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a brutal pace that causes faller or unseated incidents, reducing the race to a test of jumping accuracy and stamina at the finish.
scenarios.body: With Hatos and Mcgregors Charge committed to the front and a field of only five, any jumping error or early exit could dramatically reshape the contest. Jetty May's one win came in Good ground over an appropriate trip and Nicholls' conditional jockey angle adds intrigue, but this scenario depends on misfortune rather than form.

watchPoints.text: Hatos and Mcgregors Charge — watch the first three fences closely; if both commit hard for the lead the race will be set up as a true test of stamina and the tempo could become race-defining from the outset.
My Cullen — top weight at 168lbs is a genuine concern at 2m5f Good; if Freddie Keighley cannot secure a clean jump at the early fences from rear, ground will be lost and the weight burden amplified.

Mr McWhinny — Finn Lambert will need to make an early tactical decision about whether to chase its natural hold-up position or adapt to midfield; either choice carries risk given the horse is not operating in its preferred role.

Jetty May — 76 days off the track is worth monitoring in-running; if she travels fluently through the first mile for Paddy Hanlon she is likely to be dangerous, but if she looks laboured early the layoff may be telling.

Newton Abbot's Good surface is consistent across all six races on the card today — no hidden deterioration to factor in, and the going report shows no variance between distances, so stamina and jumping accuracy will be the truest test.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Mother Ship
runners_data.note: Front-runner clear on profile who has been racing off modest pace in recent form, going fine on Good but finishing positions have been moderate; trainer John Joseph Hanlon sends her over from Ireland suggesting confidence, and she wears a tongue piece — if she leads and dictates here she is in her comfort zone, though the STYLE_FIT flag notes she has been racing out of role lately, which tempers the authority of her finish.
runners_data.comment: Mother Ship showed well last time out with a second, though that follows a patchy run of form with little else to shout about in her last five starts; winless in recent starts and carrying 166 lb, she has run over today's trip before and represents a each-way each-way — a competitive but limited profile.

runners_data.name: Devon Red
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and profile is genuinely unknown (style=U), which injects raw uncertainty into any positioning read; showed a placed effort over 16f on Good for Nick Scholfield, steps up significantly in trip here and that stamina question is the key unknown over 2m5½f.
runners_data.comment: Devon Red has been knocking at the door, finishing second last time out just 16 days ago, and his rating of 90 marks him as a genuine threat at the weights; the risk is that he remains winless in recent starts and needs to convert his placed effort into something more decisive.

runners_data.name: Ocean Heights
runners_data.note: David Pipe's consistent stayer has placed five times in nine similar-ground runs and won once, and Jack Tudor's booking is a clear positive; racing prominently suits this trip, and his recent 2nd and 3rd over similar distances on Good establish him as the natural pick to track the leader.
runners_data.comment: Ocean Heights has shown a consistent knack for hitting the frame, finishing second two starts back and third on two of the three runs prior to that, and our rating of 91 marks him out as a strong contender here; the risk is that he remains winless in recent starts and must overcome a hefty 163 lb.

runners_data.name: Mystic Wind
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton teams up with Dan Skelton — always a potent combination — but four runs have yielded zero places on Good ground and the style is hold-up in a race unlikely to generate the pace he needs; a 50-day break also requires monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked sixth of eight on our rating, Mystic Wind faces an uphill task here; he is rated 87 by the handicapper and returns after 50 days off carrying 162 lb, so fitness under a big weight is the real question.

runners_data.name: Makinbecon
runners_data.note: Two wins from five attempts over 18-20f on Good ground give him genuine stamina credentials, and Callum Pritchard has ridden him placed before; runs in hold-up style from the rear, but with the pace likely to be steady he will need to be aggressive positioning from halfway to have any chance of closing.
runners_data.comment: Makinbecon has finished sixth in each of his last two starts, and while he does boast a win three starts back and was a winner five starts back, the overall profile places him last on our figures in an eight-runner field, making him difficult to fancy despite a quick turnaround and experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Gilded Glance
runners_data.note: Jane Williams runner has been absent 146 days — the longest layoff in the field — and his last four runs include a pulled-up and multiple tailed-off efforts; a true hold-up type pushed into the midfield map by the redistribution, his long absence and poor recent string make him the most speculative runner in the race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and pulling up most recently, Gilded Glance needs to bounce back sharply, yet a rating of 89 suggests she retains ability and a stable return after 146 days off could spark improvement — the concern is whether that layoff has left her short of match practice.

runners_data.name: Captain Connor
runners_data.note: Clare Ellam's 4-year-old has form figures that include a 2nd over 22f on Good, which is a relevant positive for this trip, but also several mid-pack finishes on softer going; a natural hold-up horse whose map position is a product of redistribution rather than tactics, and Brendan Powell will need to find a positive route through traffic if this shape quickens late.
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye with a runner-up finish last time out after a rough patch in recent starts, and Captain Connor has run over today's trip before; carrying 158 lb, he rates the one to beat on our figures despite being yet to win in his last five.

runners_data.name: Ghost Jury
runners_data.note: Kayley Woollacott's 7-year-old has ran 12 of 13 runs on Good or similar going, building a consistent staying profile, and a 2nd over 22f on Good is directly relevant form; Ben Jones rides, and while the horse is a genuine hold-up type placed into midfield by redistribution, his experience on this going and trip makes him the most credible of the redistributed trio if the race opens up.
runners_data.comment: Ghost Jury has shown she can compete, with a win and two second-place finishes in her last five starts, but ranked seventh of eight on our figures and lugging 153 lb, she faces a stiff ask, despite having run over today's trip before.

races.paceDynamic: Mother Ship is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only Ocean Heights as a secondary prominent type, she is likely to control this race from the front at a sustainable, uncontested clip over 2m5½f on Good ground. That measured gallop sets up a race where those immediately tracking her — Ocean Heights in particular — will be best placed to pounce from a close-up position without having burned reserves. The absence of genuine pace pressure means the field will bunch and travel, which structurally disadvantages hold-up horses that depend on gaps and a strung-out field to deliver their effort from deep. This race shape strongly favours hold-up-to-prominent profiles that can travel within two lengths of the leader into the straight — pure closers will find the pace insufficient to generate the momentum they need. The field holds more hold-up types than can be naturally accommodated at the rear: Ghost Jury, Captain Connor and Gilded Glance are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield map, and of those, Ghost Jury (experienced on this type of trip and going) and Captain Connor are most likely to actually secure a midfield berth, while Gilded Glance's long absence makes positioning uncertain.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Close Pursuer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Mother Ship dictates an uncontested, measured tempo and is headed approaching the final hurdle by a horse that has tracked her throughout.
scenarios.body: Mother Ship sets a comfortable gallop, keeping the field compact throughout the long back straight, and Ocean Heights — travelling prominently under Jack Tudor — slots in second before asserting from the last; the sustainable pace rewards horses that have conserved energy in the first half.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays All From Front
scenarios.trigger: If Mother Ship proves stronger than her OR suggests and quickens clear from the last to hold on.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to apply early pressure, Mother Ship luxuriates in front and, ridden to maintain rhythm rather than sprint, simply has too much in reserve when rivals challenge on the run-in; staying types that enjoy an honest but not brutal tempo benefit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Hold-Up Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough to stretch the field and a midfield runner delivers a sustained run from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Ghost Jury or Makinbecon, who possess genuine staying ability on Good ground, find daylight down the outer and peg back front-runners who have gone too soon; Makinbecon's two wins over similar trips and going make him the standout candidate for this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Collapses, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Mother Ship capitulates before the last, fracturing the race and letting a previously shuffled horse profit from the chaos.
scenarios.body: A scrambled finish ensues as multiple horses cry enough turning in, and a hold-up type — most plausibly Devon Red or Mystic Wind — finds a clear passage to pick up the pieces; this shape depends heavily on horses racing out of their natural role actually delivering, which history suggests is unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Mother Ship's early position is critical — if she is allowed to bowl along unchallenged from flag-fall, the entire race shape is set and Ocean Heights is the immediate danger tracking her.
Gilded Glance has been off 146 days and ran pulled-up last time; watch the market move (or not) as a quick guide to stable confidence before committing to any scenario involving him.

Devon Red's unknown running style means his early position cannot be predicted — if he pushes forward and applies pressure to Mother Ship, the pace context shifts and the controlled-lead scenario weakens.
Mystic Wind's hold-up style combined with a steady pace over 2m5½f means Harry Skelton will need to be creative with positioning from the home turn — watch for him moving wide early to find daylight.

Makinbecon was last seen just 10 days ago and comes here fresh enough; if Callum Pritchard hunts up sooner than expected given the likely lack of pace, it signals the stable believes a prominent ride is needed over this longer trip.
